name: Stýrivolt
description: Stýrivolt is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from the Faroe Islands, belonging to the Karnöffel group. A 48-card pack is used (tens removed from a standard French deck). Each player receives 9 cards in batches of three; 12 cards remain as stock. The dealer determines two chosen suits from the stock; cards in those suits have special powers (stikkar, lambs, taking cards). There is no requirement to follow suit. The team that wins at least five of the nine tricks wins the hand. Winning the first five tricks (vol) scores a bonus.
deck: Standard 48-card deck (tens removed from French pack). Nine cards each, 12-card stock.

history.origins: Stýrivolt descends from the German game Karnöffel and probably evolved in the early 17th century, spreading to Scandinavia; the name stýr-wålt appears in Sweden in 1658 (Georg Stiernhielm's poem Hercules). It has been played on the Faroe Islands since the 18th century and is documented in Jens Christian Svabo's travel writings (1781–1782) and in Danish game compendia from 1774 onward. The game survived as a Faroese tradition while largely disappearing from Denmark; rules were recorded in the cultural magazine Varðin (1975) and in later English-language rule publications.
timeline: Today: Still played, rules preserved orally.
history.cultural: Used chalk marks (scoring) on the table.
history.evolution: The term 'Stýrivolt' likely comes from Danish/German terms (Steuervalt? steer/rule?).

setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards to each player, 3 at a time. Twelve cards remain as stock; the dealer uses them to determine the two chosen suits.

rules.objective: Each partnership aims to win at least five of the nine tricks. The team that wins the majority scores on a chalk-up by erasing strokes; the first side to erase all three strokes (or eliminate the opponents' crosses) scores a cross. Making vol (winning the first five tricks) or taking all nine tricks scores extra.
rules.gameplay: The player to the left of the dealer leads to the first trick. Play is clockwise. Any card may be played; there is no requirement to follow suit or to beat the lead. Trick winner is determined by the game's ranking: permanent stikkar and chosen-suit stikkar beat other cards; chosen sevens (lambs) win the trick when led but cannot lead to the first trick. Whoever wins a trick leads to the next. A team that has taken five tricks may stop or continue; taking the first five (vol) or all nine scores bonus strokes.
keyRules: Two chosen suits per deal, determined by dealer from stock.
Permanent and chosen-suit stikkar outrank normal cards; lambs (chosen 7s) win when led.
Trader (chosen 5) may be exchanged for the exposed card of that suit.
Hand with no stikkar may exchange hand for the stock before the first trick is complete.

strategy.basic: Keep high cards (Aces/Kings). Since you don't have to follow suit, you can throw trash on opponent's winning trick or save an Ace for when you lead.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Vol' Attempt: If you have 5 sure winners, lead them out to win instantly without letting opponents play. Since they don't have to follow suit, they can't trump you (no trumps?).
strategy.advanced: Tracking: 16 cards are undealt. Don't rely on counting specific obscure cards, but track Aces. If all 4 Aces are gone, Kings are bosses.

variations.name: Cutting for a stikkar
variations.description: Cards are cut before the deal; the cutter may look at the bottom card of the stock. If it is a permanent stikkar, it is exposed and can be exchanged by the holder of the king of that suit before the first trick.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes only procedural rules; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Choosing suits face up
variations.description: As the dealer chooses suits, the cards turned from the stock are laid face up so everyone can see them.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes only visibility of suit selection; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Play with compulsory beating
variations.description: Every player must beat the highest card so far played to the trick if possible, unless that card was played by their partner.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation would require different play constraints; overrides not yet mapped to engine paths.

scoring.description: Chalk Marks. Vertical line with 3 cross strokes. Erase strokes as you win games. First to erase 3 strokes wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Stýrivolt is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from the Faroe Islands. 48-card deck, 9 cards each, two chosen suits; win 5 of 9 tricks.
